title: Field Operator Stabilization Procedures and Customer Briefs
author: Asha Mehta
body:
Summary:

This runbook documents a compact, operator-focused stabilization runloop for first 10–30 minutes of any service-impacting event that primarily affects inference traffic (latency spikes, KV cache evictions, model-serve OOMs, and mass rate-limit bursts). It includes a clear triage ladder, step-by-step actions for the field operator, templates for customer-facing comms, a short post-incident evidence checklist, and a game-day syllabus to keep operator skills fresh.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: Enable an on-call operator (primary or secondary) to quickly stabilize traffic, limit blast radius, and produce consistent customer status updates while evidence is collected for later RCA.
- Scope: Production incidents impacting Redwood-hosted inference API (hosted/dedicated), routing/fallbacks, KV caching layers, batch router, and model-serving runtime. Not intended for low-priority config requests or non-prod environments.

Key contacts and ownership:

- Primary operator: on-call SRE (PagerDuty escalation)
- Escalation owners: Serving Runtime (team-serving-runtime), Platform (team-platform), SRE (eng-sre), Customer Success (cs-respond), Security (security-ops)
- Slack channels: #oncall-ops (primary), #platform-alerts (secondary)
- PagerDuty escalation policy: "Inference API — Primary" -> "Inference API — Secondary" -> "SRE Shift Lead"

Severity mapping (quick reference):

1. Sev1 (Critical) — System-wide outage or p99 latency > 5s for > 5 minutes, customers experiencing failed requests or large-scale degraded throughput.
2. Sev2 (Major) — Significant latency/regression affecting a subset of customers or increased error rates (5–20% error rate sustained > 10 minutes).
3. Sev3 (Minor) — Transient errors, single-customer impact, or degradations with automated fallback in effect.

SLOs to use during triage:

- Hosted text-generation API: availability 99.95% monthly; p99 latency target < 400ms (tokens streaming excluded).
- Dedicated customer pools: throughput-based SLOs agreed per contract (reference customer SLA doc).
- KV cache hit-rate baseline: > 65% for high-read workloads; immediate declines below 40% indicate cache eviction storms.
- Error budget threshold for immediate escalation: remaining error budget < 10% for the rolling 30d window.

Operator stabilization runloop (first 10 minutes):

1) Acknowledge and collect signals (0–2 min)
   - Acknowledge PagerDuty and join bridge/Slack.
   - Record initial symptom set: service(s), region(s), observed metrics (p95/p99 latency, error rate, queue depth), and time window.
   - Commands to run immediately:
     - curl -sS https://status.redwood.com/health | jq .
     - kubectl --context=prod get pods -n inference -l app=inference-gateway -o wide | grep -E "CrashLoop|Evicted"
     - grafana quick checks: open dashboard "Inference — p99 latency by region" and snapshot if possible.

2) Contain the blast radius (2–6 min)
   - If KV cache eviction spike: temporarily reduce cache churn by throttling autoscaler for model-onboarding jobs and apply cache warming (see KV cache warm command below).
   - If p99 latency spike caused by noisy tenant: apply tenant-aware rate limit:
     - rctl set-tenant-rate --tenant-id <TENANT> --per-sec 5
   - If model-serving OOMs: switch traffic to compatible fallback model variant (policy: model-variant-fallback v1.2) via the router:
     - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/router/switch -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"redwood-compat-v1.2"}'
   - If ingress/backpressure in batch-router: decrease batch size and enable immediate draining:
     - POST /api/v1/batch-router/drain?mode=fast

3) Stabilize throughput (6–12 min)
   - Re-route a small % (5–10%) of traffic to a warm standby region or a lower-cost variant to relieve the hot path. Use canary routing when available.
     - routectl split --from inference-gateway:us-east-1 --to inference-gateway:us-west-2 --percent 10
   - Turn on additional logging for affected services for 10 minutes to capture evidence, then set back to info.

4) Customer comms and status (within 15 min)
   - Publish an initial status note (short form) within 10–15 minutes to status.redwood.com and post in #oncall-ops with copy for the Customer Success team. Use the template below.
   - If customer-impacting: escalate to CS and prepare tailored notices for top affected customers using the customer-brief template.

Short-form status template (initial):

Title: Incident — [Service] degraded in [region]\Status: Investigating\Impact: Elevated latency and 5xx errors for subset of API requests; customers may see request failures or slow responses.\ETA: Initial triage complete; further updates every 30 minutes or on change.\Owner: Asha Mehta (on-call)\Link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/<INCIDENT_ID>

Long-form customer brief (CS-ready) — example:

Subject: Service degradation affecting inference requests in us-east-1\\nHi <CustomerName>,

We’re currently investigating elevated latency and a higher-than-normal error rate that may affect inference requests to us-east-1. Our SREs have contained the issue and rerouted a portion of traffic; we expect partial stabilization within the next 30 minutes. We will provide a follow-up update with root-cause analysis and remediation steps once available.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Rerouted ~10% of traffic to us-west-2 (reduced pressure).
- Applied tenant-level rate limiting to high-volume tenants identified in the event.

If you are seeing failed requests, please provide request IDs and sample timestamps — we will prioritize debugging.

Regards,
Redwood SRE & Customer Success

Evidence collection checklist (before postmortem) — minimum required:

- Metric snapshots: p95/p99 latency, error-rate, request volume from Grafana (time window +/- 30m)
- Service logs: 10-min log slice from all affected inference-gateway pods
- Router traces: sampled traces for 5 failed requests (trace IDs)
- Deployment state: git commit hashes and rollout timestamps for any recent changes
- Eviction/OOM artifacts: kube events, node-level logs if applicable

Post-incident tasks (within 24–72 hours):

1. Create an incident record using the incident template (see below) and link evidence artifacts.
2. Run a prioritized RCA. If RCA requires cross-team investigation, assign action items and owners with due dates.
3. Check error budget implications and notify finance/product if SLA credits may be triggered.

Incident record template (to attach to postmortem):

- Incident ID: <INCIDENT_ID>
- Severity: Sev1/Sev2/Sev3
- Start / End time (UTC): <start> / <end>
- Impact summary: short paragraph
- Timeline (minute-level for first 60 minutes; coarse after): bullet list
- Evidence collected: list of saved metrics, logs, traces and links
- Corrective actions taken during incident: bullet list
- Postmortem owner: <Name>
- Action items: owner, description, due date, status

Postmortem rubric (what matters):

- Focus on facts: timeline, evidence, and decision points.
- Evaluate detection and mitigation latency: how long between signal and first containment?
- Quantify customer impact: requests impacted, customers affected, revenue/SLA exposure.
- Validate action items meet the SMART criteria and have owners + deadlines.

Runbook publishing checklist (for any change):

- Author and reviewer assigned.
- Test commands and rollback steps verified in a staging runbook drill.
- Add one example customer comm and one internal Slack snippet.
- Mark confidentiality and link to any affected cust-SLA references.

Game-day syllabus (30–60 minute labs run quarterly):

- Scenario A — KV eviction cascade: simulate eviction by saturating cache-writer job; validate throttling and cache-warm steps.
- Scenario B — Noisy tenant throttling: create synthetic traffic from tenant emulator; validate tenant-rate controls and customer notices.
- Scenario C — Model OOM fallback: intentionally trigger OOM on model-serving runtime and observe routing to compatible model variant.
- Scenario D — Multi-region partial outage: disable us-east-1 ingress and verify split routing and customer status updates.

Each game-day includes: pre-game checklist, operator roles (primary/secondary/bridge), 1-hour controlled window, and a 30-min retro capturing evidence for the postmortem template.

Escalation matrix (quick view):

- If within first 10 minutes the operator cannot reduce error rate or latency by 50%: escalate to Serving Runtime lead (pager: team-serving-runtime).
- If security artifact suspected (e.g., abnormal auth failures): escalate to Security immediately and mark confidentiality: restricted.
- If > 30 minutes without stabilization on a Sev1: notify Exec on-call and Customer Success for customer outreach.

CLI snippets and useful commands (operators):

- KV cache warm: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/cache/warm -d '{"scope":"global","keys":10}'
- Snapshot metrics to S3: curl -X POST https://metrics.redwood.internal/snapshot -d '{"dash":"inference-p99","window":"30m"}'
- Rotate inference router: routectl rotate --service inference-gateway --mode soft

Operational notes and common pitfalls:

- Avoid full rollback of serving runtime in first 15 minutes unless it's the only evident cause — prefer routing to fallbacks first.
- Don’t mass-scale down nodes during an ongoing OOM event — that can increase eviction churn.
- Always preserve raw logs before truncation for legal and compliance evidence retention.

Retention and evidence policy pointers:

- Incident artifacts required for Sev1: full logs and traces retained for 180 days.
- For Sev2: retain 90 days.
- For Sev3: retain 30 days.

Appendix: short checklist for the operator to post (single-line items):

- Acknowledge PD and join bridge
- Collect initial metrics snapshot
- Contain blast radius (rate-limit / re-route / drain)
- Publish initial status (status.redwood.com)
- Collect evidence (logs, traces, commits)
- Escalate as needed per matrix
- Create incident record and assign postmortem owner

Related pages and references: refer to dashboards and runbooks in the "eng-sre" space for detailed dashboards, and to the Customer Success sprint playbook for templated customer notifications.
